items.q: What is the correct order of the product life cycle stages in the specification?
items.why: The specification lists development, introduction, growth, maturity, decline.

items.q: In which stages of the product life cycle is cash flow from a product usually negative?
items.why: Money is spent developing and launching the product before sales build up.

items.q: Which of these is an extension strategy listed in the specification?
items.why: The specification lists advertising, rebranding, lowering the price and adapting the product.

items.q: What are the two axes of the Boston Matrix?
items.why: Products are placed by the growth of their market and their share of it.

items.q: What is a cash cow?
opts: A product with a low share in a high-growth market
A product with a high market share in a low-growth market
A product with a low share in a low-growth market
A product with a high share in a high-growth market
items.why: Cash cows earn a lot and need little spending, so they generate cash.

items.q: What is a question mark (problem child)?
opts: A product with a high share in a high-growth market
A product that is about to be withdrawn
A product with a low market share in a high-growth market
A product with a high share in a low-growth market
items.why: The market is attractive but the product has not yet won much share. It may need heavy spending to grow.

items.q: How do businesses often use the cash from their cash cows?
opts: To support question marks and stars
It must all be paid out as dividends
To lower prices on cash cows
items.why: Cash from mature products can fund products that could become the next stars or cash cows.

items.q: What is a dog?
opts: A product with a low share in a high-growth market
A product with a low market share in a low-growth market
A product with a high share in a low-growth market
items.why: Dogs often earn little and may be dropped, although some still make a profit or support other products.

items.q: What is one of the main challenges of new product development?
opts: It is expensive and many new products fail
items.why: NPD needs research, design and testing, and there is no guarantee customers will buy the result.

items.q: What is one value of new product development?
opts: It guarantees a higher share price
It creates new sources of revenue to replace products in decline
It means the business no longer needs marketing
items.why: New products can keep the business competitive as older products reach maturity and decline.

items.q: What is price skimming?
opts: Setting a high price at launch and lowering it over time
Setting a low price to win market share quickly
Changing price with demand in real time
items.why: Skimming targets customers who will pay more to have the product first.

items.q: What is penetration pricing?
opts: Setting a high price at launch
Setting a low price at launch to win market share quickly
items.why: The low price attracts customers fast. The price may rise once the product is established.

items.q: Which of these is an example of dynamic pricing?
opts: Train fares that change depending on how many seats are left and when you book
A supermarket matching a rival's price
A product priced at £9.99 instead of £10
items.why: Dynamic pricing changes prices in response to demand, often automatically using data.

items.q: What is cost-based pricing?
opts: Adding a mark-up to the cost of making the product
Setting the price at the same level as rivals
items.why: It is simple and makes sure each unit covers its cost, but it ignores what customers will pay.

items.q: What is going rate pricing?
opts: Setting the highest price in the market
Setting a price similar to rivals' prices
Setting a price that changes every hour
items.why: Going rate pricing is common where products are similar and customers compare prices.

items.q: Under which method of pricing does the specification list premium pricing?
items.why: The specification lists premium, going rate and discount as competition-based methods.

items.q: When is price skimming most likely to work?
opts: When there are many identical rivals
When the business wants market share quickly
When demand is very price elastic
When the product is new or unique and some customers will pay a lot to have it first
items.why: Skimming needs customers who are not very sensitive to price, which is more likely when there is little competition.

items.q: What is one risk of penetration pricing?
opts: It always leads to a loss
Low margins, and customers may resist when the price is raised later
items.why: The business earns little on each unit, and customers who joined for the low price may leave when it rises.

items.q: Which of these is an influence on price listed in the specification?
items.why: The specification lists marketing objectives, target market, level of demand, PED, costs, competitors' actions and the marketing mix.

items.q: A business raises its price and its costs stay the same. What happens to the profit margin on each unit?
items.why: The gap between price and cost per unit gets bigger, although the business may sell fewer units.
